Sampling variances of a planned trial

Source: R/design.R
neyman_variance.Rd

Computes the planning approximation of the sampling variance of each site's impact estimate in an individually randomized multisite trial.

Usage

neyman_variance(n, p = 0.5, R2 = 0, var_outcome = 1)

Arguments

n

Planned numbers of individuals in the sites, a numeric vector of positive numbers.

p

Proportion of each site's individuals assigned to treatment, numbers strictly between 0 and 1, one for all sites or one per site.

R2

Proportion of the outcome variance explained by covariates, numbers in \([0, 1)\), one for all sites or one per site.

var_outcome

Variance of the outcome within each arm of a site (\(s_j^2\) in equation 2 of Lee, 2026), positive numbers, one for all sites or one per site.

Value

A numeric vector of sampling variances, one per site.

Details

The variance of a difference in means with covariate adjustment is approximately $$v_j = \Big(\frac{1}{p_j} + \frac{1}{1 - p_j}\Big)\frac{s_j^2 (1 - R^2)}{n_j} = \frac{\kappa_j}{n_j}$$ (Lee, 2026, equation 2). The argument names are those of multisiteDGP::compute_kappa(). Designs with blocks, clusters or other estimators need their own variance formula; reliability_design() also takes the constants \(\kappa_j\) directly.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

Examples

neyman_variance(c(20, 50, 100))
#> [1] 0.20 0.08 0.04
neyman_variance(c(20, 50, 100), p = 0.6, R2 = 0.4)
#> [1] 0.125 0.050 0.025
